_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (master_data): Number ranges must be separated for NewCo so that new records are easy to spot after go-live.

Verbatim from the workshop: "number ranges to be separated for NewCo so that new records are easy to spot after go-live"

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-MD-002 — Number ranges and groupings for master data [master_data]
Standard process: Master data objects draw their keys from number range intervals. An interval is either internal, meaning the system assigns the next number, or external, meaning the user or a loading program supplies the key. Intervals are assigned to a grouping or type, so different categories of the same object can be numbered separately. When a new legal entity is stood up, giving it its own intervals so that its records do not collide with those of the parent is a matter of defining intervals and assigning them to the relevant groupings. This is customizing content and needs no code.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Internal and external number assignment per object.; Multiple intervals per object, assigned by grouping, account group, or type.; Buffering and gap behaviour for high-volume assignment.
Common configuration points: Number range object intervals, including from-number, to-number, and external flag.; Assignment of intervals to business partner groupings, material types, and document types.; Separate intervals per company code or per organizational unit where the object supports it.
Typically beyond the standard: Key formats that encode business meaning the number range object cannot express.; Renumbering existing records while preserving references, which is a migration build.

### KB-XC-003 — Thresholds, approver assignment, code lists, and number ranges are customizing content [cross_cutting]
Standard process: A large share of the behaviour that business users perceive as bespoke is in fact table-driven. Monetary limits that decide whether an approval step is required, the number of approval levels, which role approves at which level, the intervals from which document numbers are drawn, and the sets of permitted reason or status codes are all maintained as customizing values. Changing them alters behaviour without touching code, and the delivered logic reads them at runtime. The correct question to ask about such a requirement is not whether the value is unusual, but whether the delivered logic already reads a value of that kind from a table.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Delivered release and approval logic evaluates limits and characteristics maintained in customizing.; Number assignment reads intervals from number range objects.; Permitted values for coded fields are maintained as check tables.
Common configuration points: Value limits per approval level and the assignment of approvers to levels.; Number range intervals, internal versus external assignment, and their assignment to groupings.; Reason codes, blocking reasons, status profiles, and document types.; Field status controls that make a delivered field required, optional, or suppressed.
Typically beyond the standard: Approval routing that depends on an attribute the delivered logic cannot read as a characteristic.; Making a field mandatory when that field is not part of the delivered object.

### KB-R2R-001 — Record-to-report end-to-end standard flow [R2R]
Standard process: Financial accounting posts journal entries to the general ledger, either automatically from operational documents or manually. Documents carry a document type, a posting date, and a period, and the delivered period control decides whether a period is open for a given account type. Open items on customer, supplier, and general ledger accounts are cleared against each other. Period close runs recurring entries, accruals, revaluation, and reconciliation, and financial statements are produced from a financial statement version that arranges accounts into the required hierarchy. Running the ledger, posting journals, closing periods, clearing open items, and producing statements is delivered behaviour.
Capabilities covered by the standard: General ledger posting from operational documents and manual journals.; Open item management and automatic clearing.; Period open and close control per account type and per company code.; Financial statement versions and the reports built on them.; Parallel ledgers and currencies.
Common configuration points: Document types and their number ranges.; Posting period variants and which periods are open for which account types.; Automatic clearing rules and tolerance groups.; Financial statement version hierarchies.
Typically beyond the standard: Statement structures that the financial statement version cannot express.; Recurring bespoke extracts whose layout is defined by a receiving system.

### KB-P2P-004 — Sourcing, contracts, and info records [P2P]
Standard process: The delivered sourcing content determines where a requisition is sourced from. Purchasing info records hold the supplier-material relationship and its conditions, outline agreements hold negotiated terms and release quantities, and the source list can restrict or fix which supplier may be used for a material at a plant. Quota arrangements distribute demand across several suppliers by percentage. Source determination during requisition and order creation reads this content and proposes or fixes the supplier. All of it is master data and customizing; none of it requires code.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Purchasing info records with price conditions and planned delivery time.; Outline agreements including quantity and value contracts and scheduling agreements.; Source list and quota arrangement driven source determination.; Automatic supplier proposal during requisition conversion.
Common configuration points: Whether a source list is mandatory for a plant.; Condition types and pricing procedures used in purchasing.; Document types for outline agreements.
Typically beyond the standard: Source determination driven by a score or rating maintained outside the ERP system.; Sourcing rules that cannot be expressed as source list, quota, or contract content.

parsed.rationale: KB-MD-002 explicitly states: 'When a new legal entity is stood up, giving it its own intervals ... is a matter of defining intervals and assigning them to the relevant groupings. This is customizing content and needs no code.' KB-XC-003 confirms number range intervals are customizing content. Separating number ranges for NewCo is therefore a configuration activity requiring no code.
